html:
Jean Rhys was a novelist born in Roseau, Dominica, in 1890, to a Welsh father and a white Creole mother. She left for England at sixteen and spent most of her life in Europe.

Her early novels of the 1920s and 1930s tell of lonely women drifting in Paris and London. After years of silence she wrote Wide Sargasso Sea (1966), which gives a life to the mad wife in Charlotte Bronte's Jane Eyre: a Creole heiress from Jamaica and Dominica.

The book is now read as a classic of postcolonial writing, telling the old story from the Caribbean side, in the world after emancipation. She stands with Derek Walcott among the island writers known worldwide.
